*** We may want to {color:#4c9aff}*update the privacy notice section on this*{color}, just to make it clear.
** The data being collected here appears proportionate / not intrusive.
* *Legal basis:*
** This concerns setting prices, so you could argue contractual necessity here. However, the price is between the driver and the passenger (as much as it is partly determined by Bolt).
** IMO, it would be worth {color:#4c9aff}*conducting a LIA*{color} just to be on the safe side, as Bolt has a legitimate interest in implementing this feature (flexible pricing helps connect drivers and passengers, and benefits both of them(.
* *ADM:*
** The only ‘new element’ of this is the offers / counter-offers (i.e., setting the baseline price and blast dispatching to drivers are separate and already happening). This is done by the users, and so would not count as ADM.
** However, if price bids are fed into the price setting algorithm and influence base estimates over time, then we would need to {color:#ff5630}*consider this more carefully*{color}.
*** e.g., If a passenger frequently offers lower prices, the algorithm might automatically show them higher minimum fares in the future. Alternatively, if a driver rejects too many lower bids, the algorithm might deprioritise them in receiving trip offers. We need to make sure this does not happen.
*** We could still argue that users have control over the final bid (but this would be within a certain range, as determined by the baseline fare, so be careful).
* *Transparency:*
** As mentioned above, need to slightly tweak the relevant row of the privacy notice.
** We will be publishing guidance materials on how price bidding works, which will go some way to keeping this feature transparent.
* *Backend / DSRRs:*
** As mentioned above, we need to check how much of this data we are keeping, as we may need to consider whether we can provide it in response to DSARs.
*** If we do have a good reason to retain it, we should ensure that: (i) users can request a copy; and (ii) we can delete it (if after an assessment we detrmine that we should).
** A recommendable retention period may be for 30 ays after the trip is finished, unless required for disputes or fraud prevention.

{panel:bgColor=#deebff}
*Conclusion*
{panel}

* No obvious blockers from a Privacy POV.
* In terms of Privacy action items:
** Check whether a PPRA has already been done on this (Alon).
** Consider whether an LIA is required (or the current price setting LIA needs to be updated).
** Update the privacy notice, and ensure links are provided at the relevant times.
* Business action items:
** Ensure guidance materials are published on how price bidding works.
** Ensure that this data does not result in any profiling of users., nor affect the baseline pricing algorithm / work allocation.
* Questions:
** Any changes to how eligible drivers are found? I assume not.
** Would previous bids remain visible to users in their app?
** Will this influence price estimates / pricing algorithms over time?
** Will we be retaining details about bids / counter-offers? If so, why? Will this be used for other purposes (e.g., analysing pricing trends)?

h3. {color:#6554c0}Deep dive outcome: {color}

*Main scenarios [descending]:*

* *Unknown charge*: User noticed unknown charges on their payment method, usually from a different user account
* *Unknown orders:* User received receipts or see orders in their inapp history that they didn’t make 
* *New login:* User got an email notification about new sign-in that they don’t recognise
* *Unsolicited emails:* User is getting emails that are not connected to their account, usually the user doesn’t a have an account with Bolt at all
* *Stolen phone:* Rider’s phone was stolen and logging out the devices doesn’t help, since the fraud user has access to the phone number 
* *Driver phishing*: Account compromised due to driver requesting rider’s credentials 
* *User logged out*: User can’t sign back in because fraudster changed the credentials 
* *Phone number used on driver account:* User is complaining that their phone number is used on a driver account that they don’t own (confirm with identity how this may happen) 

*Insights:*

h1. Backend Flow

h3. Courier app sends the data

Courier app sends the data through {{/deliveryCourier/polling}}
We will have to add the new fields to {{CourierPollRequest}} [here| https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/1aca8c245ba9f8914813d75915a596866d849eb6/src/delivery/order/delivery_polling/main/service/CourierPollingService.ts#L202 ].

h3. Data reaches the backend

The {{delivery-polling}} service does the following:

* [creates|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/283f3c5c3a28d2a8f8b4ecc109111e240f5056f8/src/delivery/order/delivery_polling/main/cron/CourierLocationCacheUpdaterCron.ts#L58] a {{CourierLocationCacheRow}} object and stores it in a local dictionary indexed by courier_id. This does mean that subsequent calls that are not flushed will be overwritten. But the cron probably runs more frequently than the polling frequency.
* a cron that runs every half a second [does|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/15f387e7757ad6024387bddd48d086ef866bc555/src/delivery/order/delivery_polling/main/buffer/CourierLocationCache.ts#L68] the following:
** flushes this data to Redis (the data will be interrogated by clients)
** puts this data on a message queue {{CourierLocationMqPublisher}}

We will have to do the following:

* Update {{CourierLocationCacheRow}}  [https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/15f387e7757ad6024387bddd48d086ef866bc555/src/delivery/order/delivery_polling/main/buffer/CourierLocationCache.ts#L11|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/15f387e7757ad6024387bddd48d086ef866bc555/src/delivery/order/delivery_polling/main/buffer/CourierLocationCache.ts#L11]  to include the new fields
* Update protobuf definitions [https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/29571d3bd4adbaa2be7baf3edd3b95afcc08a514/common/parsers/tracking/proto/courierLocationEvent.proto#L1|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/29571d3bd4adbaa2be7baf3edd3b95afcc08a514/common/parsers/tracking/proto/courierLocationEvent.proto#L1]  to include the new fields
* Update parsers (e.g. buildCourierLocationChunk method) [https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/b7ebc57fadfbcbfe02cd229a76b6b84f30b27bf0/common/parsers/tracking/CourierLocationsParser.ts#L64|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/b7ebc57fadfbcbfe02cd229a76b6b84f30b27bf0/common/parsers/tracking/CourierLocationsParser.ts#L64]  

Related PR: [https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/pull/11545/files|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/pull/11545/files] 

h3. Tracking service receives the  data

The {{tracking-courier-polling}} service subscribes to {{CourierLocationMqSubscriberMqApi}}  and [processes|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/0ef1bc1230d0c24066ef0c9debd5651fed5c90ac/src/platform/geo/tracking/main/tracking_courier_polling/controller/InternalController.ts#L37] the events.

Each location is [encoded|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/a160c37eec2a93e1426f8a1ddc5aaa7dd6b92a7d/src/platform/geo/tracking/main/tracking_courier_polling/service/codecs/CourierPolledLocationCodec.ts#L103] again in a tracking-specific protobuf {{CourierPolledLocationMessage}} [https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/fb47a3640134e626f0c8a10f14816e46a5078257/src/platform/geo/tracking/main/tracking_courier_polling/store/message/CourierPolledLocationMessage.proto#L1|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/fb47a3640134e626f0c8a10f14816e46a5078257/src/platform/geo/tracking/main/tracking_courier_polling/store/message/CourierPolledLocationMessage.proto#L1]  and [stored|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/d701a22b1c20619d440bc86a2bf3d7b2c294dbb4/src/platform/geo/tracking/main/common/store/Storer.ts#L69] in a ShortTermStorage.

There is an internal endpoint {{/internal/v1/courier/getLocations}} invoked by {{delivery-courier-tracking}}, which expects a {{CourierLocationSQS}} [object|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/528943833a11fca34a92e576649b5c51b02d989a/src/platform/geo/tracking/main/tracking_courier_polling/service/TrackingCourierPollingService.ts#L151 ] as a result.
Should we expose this new telemetry data to this client (probably no since this is only invoked for active orders in admin-panel)? In any case we should update [this|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/a160c37eec2a93e1426f8a1ddc5aaa7dd6b92a7d/src/platform/geo/tracking/main/tracking_courier_polling/service/codecs/CourierPolledLocationCodec.ts#L55] {{decode}} function.

A cron periodically reads from the short term storage and [publishes|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/5b71697aad92f10ea7edefae1270f71b330062b4/src/platform/geo/tracking/main/common/cron/FileIndexerCron.ts#L166 ] the partition keys that need to be synced to S3 on a queue.

A worker service [listens|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/ba6d11c95169f6078156f6263eec8ccad53e8219/src/platform/geo/tracking/main/tracking_courier_polling/BootstrapFileSyncerWorker.ts#L64] to events published on that queue and moves the data from Redis to S3.

The data is stored as a {{CourierPolledLocation}} [object|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/05a1e667e0cfdba15e2c09cbdb3b869f35fbc56a/src/platform/geo/tracking/main/tracking_courier_polling/service/codecs/CourierPolledLocation.ts#L3 ].

We'll also have to update protobuf [definitions|https://github.com/bolteu/spark/blob/da14903d3655fa40c5c6b30fbe19256ad2e35255/common/src/main/java/ee/mtakso/spark/common/data/rides/models/dtos/proto/CourierPolledLocationMessageOuterClass.java#L8], BUT (per [~accountid:5fa5127814da260068321c34]) make sure to use libprotoc 2.6.1 to generate them.

Let me briefly explain the situation with FinReg risk and why we are taking time to look into early cashout rollout in more detail for Canada. In Canada, we operate under a very distinct and detailed payment regulation which extends to a broad range of businesses, including also marketplace platforms. Relying on the Airwallex solution helps us to comply with such local licensing laws and our *core/basic setup* of collecting payments and disbursing payouts under the current Airwallex solution is deemed sufficient at this time for regulatory compliance. 

However, even with relying on Airwallex, in case of Canada with its rather unique regulation, we still need to apply additional risk mitigations to stay outside the payments licensing requirements. With additional payments related features/services which we want to roll out, we will need to be able to show that those features are *incidental to our main service* of providing ride-hailing marketplace - that the functions we are offering are performed only because they are _necessary_ to the non-payment service or business activity (ride-hailing platform provision). One of the conditions which points to it being not incidental, is the platform charging the customer for these features (if platform “generates revenues or commercial advantages” from payment related features of the platform). So with our intention to charge the drivers an early cashout fee (which as I understand would be higher than merely the cost paid to AWX), I see that with charging the fee we may potentially fall out of the safe zone of being outside of the licensing requirement. 

I would like to run this risk by [~accountid:624469dd45ece00069c967bd] as well, she will be back from vacation next week. I am then able to provide final FinReg opinion on the early cashouts in Canada.

h2. GPS accuracy, bearing, altitude, speed


These we can get from [https://transistorsoft.github.io/react-native-background-geolocation/interfaces/location.html|https://transistorsoft.github.io/react-native-background-geolocation/interfaces/location.html|smart-link], which is the package currently used by the Courier App
Check [this|https://github.com/bolteu/food-delivery-courier-app/blob/03a829c4c1c866e8925d6493a3bd4da97b0c9a2b/src/rdx/isGpsEnabled/epics/updateGpsStateEpic.ts#L14 ] for a starting point.

Open question re: altitude - should we use {{altitude}} or {{ellipsoidal_altitude}}?

Any reason why the {{heading}} field isn’t sent to the backend already?

h2. Proximity sensor

We could use this package
[https://github.com/kibolho/react-native-proximity-sensor|https://github.com/kibolho/react-native-proximity-sensor], but it seems that it's not very popular
Alternative is to write it from scratch.

Caveat: on iOS the sensor returns a boolean, while on Android the distance is b/w 0 and 10 cm

h2. Light sensor

This [https://docs.expo.dev/versions/latest/sdk/light-sensor/|https://docs.expo.dev/versions/latest/sdk/light-sensor/|smart-link]    would work, but can we do it since the Courier App hasn't migrated to expo yet?

An alternative could be this [https://www.npmjs.com/package/react-native-ambient-light-sensor|https://www.npmjs.com/package/react-native-ambient-light-sensor|smart-link] (but not very popular). or we can write our own native module like [here|https://medium.com/engineering-at-bajaj-health/creating-a-surrounding-light-sensor-module-for-android-device-in-react-native-6a0f9fa7d13e].

h2. Temperature and humidity sensors

Could not find a package that exposes this, although it looks it could be pretty straight-forward to add support here [https://github.com/react-native-sensors/react-native-sensors|https://github.com/react-native-sensors/react-native-sensors|smart-link]

OTOH, the project seems to be [abandoned|https://github.com/react-native-sensors/react-native-sensors/issues/466].

h2. Wi-fi /cellular signal strength

This [https://www.npmjs.com/package/@react-native-community/netinfo|https://www.npmjs.com/package/@react-native-community/netinfo|smart-link]  package exposes a bunch of network-related information. It looks like we could find out the connection type (wi-fi / cellular), wi-fi strength, as well as cellular network type (2g/3g/4g/5g) without requiring additional permissions.

+*BACKGROUND*+

* On 29 March 2025, a rider ([profile|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/identity/consumers/rider/171825215/overview]) messaged Bolt in-app ([here|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/546303812]) about an unrecognised charge on their card (EUR 13.20), based on a trip taken in Lithuania. Rider claims they have never been to Lithuania.
** Rider suspects account overlap, and notes they can see the other user’s trips.
** Unsurprisingly, CS do not understand the issue and have not been helpful to the user. the User is now threatening to complain. The rider is claiming our data security is not up to standard.
** Rider claims they created their Bolt account on 23 August 2024. However, CS noted that the account at-issue was created in 2023. Rider notes that:
*** _I created my account using my phone number not my email address_
*** _The trips happened in 2023 were not done by me. When I first registered, they were there_
*** _When I registered the APP, there was another user’s name and email. Then I changed them_
* CS separately noted a separate account recently created ([here|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/identity/consumers/rider/257741630/overview]) with the same device id (b463b674-6f10-4940-9381-ac7485a80e9f) and payment method (6337). From SD ticket description:
** A ‘fake’ user made a Bolt account in Lithuania in 2023 using the current rider’s email address on 8 May 2023.
** Rider then created a Bolt in France on 23/08/2024.
* Based on internal investigation:
** Current rider account ([here|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/identity/consumers/rider/171825215/overview]) was created in 2023 under the email [serpikov.yura@yandex.ru|mailto:serpikov.yura@yandex.ru], phone number +33745111443 and name Юрий Серпиков.
*** Details changed on 23 August 2024 to Xinyi Xu, [xinyi.xu.chine@gmail.com|mailto:xinyi.xu.chine@gmail.com]. This was the rider gaining access to this account using the phone number +33745111443.
*** Only one trip taken on the account on 29 March 2025, which matches the ‘unrecognised’ trip that the rider is complaining about.
*** Payment method ending in 6867 (confirmed as the rider’s, and used to pay for the trip at-issue) was added to the account on 23/08/2024. Before that, it was a card ending in 6337.
** Other rider account ([here|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/identity/consumers/rider/257741630/overview]) created on 30 March 2025 with name Юрий Серпиков, email [serpikov.yura@yandex.ru|mailto:serpikov.yura@yandex.ru] and phone number +353876299158.
*** This account has the 6337 payment method on it.

+*ANALYSIS*+

* I am not sure this is a case of a ‘fake account’ - I think this conclusion is too hasty. Instead, I think this is a case of *phone number recycling*:
** Юрий Серпиков (“*User 1*”) originally created [+this account+|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/identity/consumers/rider/171825215/overview] (“*Account 1*”) in 2023 using phone number +33745111443 (the “*Phone Number*”) and payment method ending in 6337 (“*Payment Method 1*”).
** In 2024, the Phone Number was reallocated to Xinyi Xu (“*User 2*”). User 2 gained access to Account 1 and changed the name and email address to their own. They also added their own payment method ending in 6867 (“*Payment Method 2*”).
** It seems that User 1 still had access to Account 1 while this was happening. As such, they were able to take one trip on Account 1 using Payment Method 2. This was the trip that User 2 was notified about.
*** It is unclear how User 1 still had access - check this.
** One day later on 30 March, User 1 created a [+new account+|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/identity/consumers/rider/257741630/overview] (“*Account 2*”) under their new phone number, and original name / email address.
* There are two personal data breaches that happened here:
** User 1’s data: User 2 had access to their account since August 2024. Was able to see previous trips etc.
** User 2’s data: User 1 was able to take a trip using Payment Method 2.
* I have reported this to the ODPO team [here|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C0678KJ49UH/p1743775868975389], as this is a confirmed data breach.
** Unlikely to be reportable IMO. No malicious intent, and financial detriment is minimal. However, technically it is ongoing.

+*NEXT STEPS*+

* Get CS / auth team to confirm my version of events. In particular:
** How did User 1 still have access?
** Is this no longer ongoing now that User 1 has set up a new account?
*** I have asked these questions [here|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C06R63EQ6CS/p1743774480597659].
* Await ODPO conclusion.
* Once analysis is confirmed by stakeholders, we should take the following steps:
** Write to User 2 explaining what happened (i.e., they got a phone number from recycling, and we will have to delete the account to stop the incident from being ongoing - the risk here is minimised, as the only recent trip was in March), delete the account, and recommend they set up a new one.
** Write to User 1 explaining what has happened, and offer then a copy of their data if they want it (redacted).

			  FROM ng_customer_support.support_comp_eligibility_request_log AS rl
			  WHERE cast(rl.created_date as date) >= date('2024-09-01')
			  AND JSON_EXTRACT_SCALAR(rl.request , '$.gmv_model.user_persona') = 'driver'
			  --AND JSON_EXTRACT_SCALAR(rl.result_fraud_check  , '$.result') = 'verify'
		      --and cast(JSON_EXTRACT_SCALAR(rl.request , '$.fraud_check.order_handle.order_id') as int) = 1708230640
		  	 ) 
		where rn = 1		
),
compensation_amount as (
		select
			  support_case_id
			, case when is_legacy_automation_compensation = true then 'automation_compensation'
				 when is_ai_compensation = true then 'ai_compensation'
				 when is_legacy_automation_compensation = false and is_ai_compensation = false then 'agent_compensation'
				 end as compensation_type
			, array_agg(distinct beehive_compensation_size_type) as compensation_rate
			, sum(compensation_amount_eur) as compensation_amount_eur --->>>>> CAN'T find cases with multiple compensations
		from customer_support_models.int_beehive_driver_compensations
		where date_trunc('month',action_created_date_utc) >= date('2024-09-01')
		group by 1,2--,3
		order by 1 desc,3
),
issue_key as ( 
		select
		  support_case_id
		--, array_agg(issue_key) as issue_keys
		from ng_customer_support.fact_support_case_issue_keys
		where issue_key in (
				'cancellation_fee_not_received',
				'rider_cancelled_order',
				'driver_rider_cancelling_active_order',
				'driver_rider_didnt_show_up',
				'rider_did_not_pay',
				'driver_rider_didnt_pay_full_price',
				'driver_mess_in_car',
				'driver_branding_bonus_not_received',
				'total_fare_too_low',
				'driver_toll_fee_missing',
				'driver_parking_fee_missing',
				'driver_wrong_destination',
				'driver_rider_chose_wrong_location',
				'issues_with_bonus',
				'driver_early_cashout_miscalculated',
				'driver_payout_miscalculated'
			    )
		and cast(support_case_created_date as date) >= date('2024-09-01')
		group by 1
		order by 1
)
-------- AGGREGATIONS ---------
select 
	  date_trunc('month',fsc.support_case_created_date_utc) as month_dt
	, c.country_name as country
	, case when fsca.is_solved_by_ai = true then 'automation' --fsc.support_case_id
		   when fsca.is_solved_by_legacy = true then 'automation' --fsc.support_case_id
		   when fsc.is_support_case_escalated_to_agent = true then 'agent' -- fsc.support_case_id
		   end as solved_type
	, case when fsca.is_solved_by_ai = true then 'ai' --fsc.support_case_id
		   when fsca.is_solved_by_legacy = true then 'legacy' --fsc.support_case_id
		   when fsc.is_support_case_escalated_to_agent = true then 'agent' -- fsc.support_case_id
		   end as solved_by
	, fc.fraud_decision
	, case when fc.fraud_decision = 'pass' and ca.compensation_amount_eur > 0 then 'pass_compensated'
		   when fc.fraud_decision = 'pass' and ca.compensation_amount_eur is null then 'pass_not_compensated'
		   when fc.fraud_decision = 'verify' and ca.compensation_amount_eur > 0 then 'verify_compensated'
		   when fc.fraud_decision = 'verify' and ca.compensation_amount_eur is null then 'verify_not_compensated'
		   when fc.fraud_decision = 'reject' and ca.compensation_amount_eur > 0 then 'reject_compensated'
		   when fc.fraud_decision = 'reject' and ca.compensation_amount_eur is null then 'reject_not_compensated'
		   when fc.fraud_decision is null and ca.compensation_amount_eur is not null then 'no_fraud_check_compensated'
		   when fc.fraud_decision is null and ca.compensation_amount_eur is null then 'no_fraud_check_not_compensated'
		   else fc.fraud_decision end as fraud_decision_comp
	, ca.compensation_rate
	, sum(ca.compensation_amount_eur) as compensation_amount
	, count(distinct fsc.support_case_id) as total_cases
/* ---- DATABASE / estructure -----------
	  fsc.support_case_id
	, fsc.support_case_created_date_utc 
	, fsc.support_case_order_id
	, c.country_name as country
	--, fsc.is_support_case_escalated_to_agent as is_solved_by_agent -->> check w/ @Masha if is safe to affrim escalated to Agent = TRUE,  then is solved by the agent
	--, fsca.is_solved_by_ai
	--, fsca.is_solved_by_automation
	, fc.fraud_decision
	, ca.compensation_amount_eur
	--, ik.issue_keys
	, case when fsc.is_support_case_escalated_to_agent = TRUE then 'agent' 
		   when fsca.is_solved_by_ai = true then 'ai'
		   when fsca.is_solved_by_automation = true then 'automation'
		   end as solved_by
	, case when ca.is_ai_compensation = true then 'ai_compensation'
		   when ca.is_legacy_automation_compensation = true then 'automation_compensation'
		   when ca.is_ai_compensation = false and ca.is_legacy_automation_compensation = false then 'manual_compensation'
		   end as compensation_trigger_process */
from core_models.fact_support_case fsc
right join issue_key as ik on fsc.support_case_id = ik.support_case_id
left join core_models.dim_city as c on c.city_id = fsc.support_case_city_id 
left join compensation_amount as ca on ca.support_case_id = fsc.support_case_id
left join fraud_check as fc on fc.support_case_id = fsc.support_case_id and fc.city_id = fsc.support_case_city_id
left join core_models.fact_support_case_automation as fsca on fsca.support_case_id = fsc.support_case_id 
	and fsca.support_case_created_date_utc >= date('2024-09-01')
where 1=1
	and fsc.support_case_user_persona = 'driver'
	and fsc.support_case_state != 'draft'
	and fsc.support_case_created_date_utc >= date('2024-09-01')
group by 1,2,3,4,5,6,7--,8--,9
order by 1,2,3,4,5,6,7{code}

If they were to initiate legal proceedings against Bolt for damages or losses they claim to have incurred, we would need to prove their *deliberate intent to harm* Bolt  and provide evidence of actual loss or damage suffered by Bolt as a direct result of their conduct.

[~accountid:712020:a7a7d4bc-10ca-44a0-a22e-fa8752330abd], privacy-wise, we allow fleet managers to input passengers' names and phone numbers and use them internally.

25W13 The problem with the dataset in Admin having duplicate or irrelevant brand traits has been addressed by [Oleh Demkiv|mailto:oleg.demkiv@bolt.eu]. We will proceed with migrating merchants to PIM.

Considering we have now extended the Airtable subscription for the next 12 months, we are not in a rush to move our operations to PIM. We will instead work on it until the overall process efficiency in PIM is same or better as in Airtable. We will be continuously testing PIM on a small scale throughout the development cycle in order to ensure a constant flow of feedback shared by people that are using PIM in their daily routine.

25W11 A/B test has been started on the 04.02 (details [+here+|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C05PRJ0RR4M/p1738175324468999]). We've split providers 50/50 between treatment and control. We intended to run the test for 4 weeks to identify if assigning tags automatically based on the statistics of the items sold (or items on the menu for providers that don't have sufficient sales data accumulated) bring better search to order conversion. However, we had to stop the test on the 27th of February after discovering that there was a bug that crashed the app for some users in specific cases (details [+here+|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C05PRJ0RR4M/p1740672072771989]).

It made us restart the test, which we did on the 4th of March. It will run now for the next 4 weeks until we can check the data and make a call on the outcomes.

25W13 [Alexandru-Mihai Șuhan|mailto:alex.suhan@bolt.eu] is working on integrating the solution into the onboarding flow so that when a menu file is stored in SF we process it through the OCR. We are currently blocked by the problem with the SF API keys and need support from the CE team.

25W13 [~accountid:62b2cf2c99eafa602d88ec9e]  and [~accountid:623ace2d7910a200718aec2d] aligned on the way Menu A/B testing will work. We are looking to support testing different prices, images, and descriptions for the MVP with automatic transformers supporting A/B tests' consistency when the control version of the menu is changed during the test by the merchant.

This re-alignment as well as some urgent on-duty tasks have pushed the completion of the tech design document back. Keeping the project completion date as is for the time being, but cosidering it may also shift as the initial stage of the project takes longer, than planned.

25W13 We have aligned on the path forward with Legal. [~accountid:5cca9996e494c810153b1b03]  will add a new paragraph to the T&Cs to reflect that we expect merchants to only share photos and other copyright-protected content with us if they own it. This is scheduled to happen in April.

The test in AZ [+has demonstrated+|https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1te1OybJQfsLe6fGCQJtIJv8nDNtn5E4UmfOVe7yvLbs/edit?gid=0#gid=0] that the system works well and is helpful. We've [+added RO to the test+|https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1te1OybJQfsLe6fGCQJtIJv8nDNtn5E4UmfOVe7yvLbs/edit?gid=606314320#gid=606314320] on the 25.03 and will work with the team's feedback to identify issues and areas for improvement.

25W13 Project is on pause at the moment, no work is being done. The markets already launched (LT, LV, PL, AZ) are running but building an automated quality control system for translations or adding a different tool to make certain problematic language pairs (like AZ-RU) work better will require us to dedicate development capacity and run it as a new project. It has not been planned for Q1 and we don't have capacity for this either on the DS or Eng side. 

We've planned it for Q2 for the Menu team.

25W13 Before we get to this project, we need to be able to run proper A/B tests on a provider level instead of a flaky before-after comparison. [~accountid:712020:39b8bb67-9df8-45af-b75f-41510d7a5284]  and [~accountid:623ace2d7910a200718aec2d] will collaborate to make it happen.

The manual test will still be done by OPS in the meanwhile where the menus will be enriched by images.

25W13 Project was put on hold based on the results of the OPS quality review done in 2024. We are looking at restarting it in Q1, this time using a proper A/B testing setup to judge the impact. A necessary prerequisite for this is the support for menu A/B testing on a provider level.

In a *microservice architecture*, services should be loosely coupled and support *backward compatibility*.

If multiple packages *must be deployed or reverted together in a specific order*, this signals *tight coupling* between services, which goes against microservice best practices.

By supporting the whole feature (auto-suggesting cross-package reverts), we implicitly *encourage bad design patterns*, like:

* Services depend on *each other’s internal versions*,

* Lack of *clear version boundaries* or contracts,

* Fragile release chains make services harder to evolve independently.

Instead, we should use this as a *feedback signal*:

{quote}If you can’t safely roll back one service alone, your architecture may need decoupling or stronger compatibility guarantees.{quote}

Both methods rely on the *same fundamental data*: a list of cohorts ranked by their estimated marketing efficiency.

However, they differ in *how they use this data*:

# *The Static LPCT Playbook:* This takes the ranked efficiency data and pre-packages it into fixed rows or increments. This is a "one-off" creation process.
# *The Automation (Dynamic Budget Targeting):* This uses the same efficiency ranking but performs a calculation ("binary search") _each time_ it runs for a specific market and budget. It dynamically finds the best set of campaigns from the ranked list to precisely match the given budget constraint for that specific instance.

*The result:* While both aim for the same goal (optimizing campaigns based on efficiency) using the same base data, the _representation_ and _application_ are different. The dynamic automation approach can create campaign sets that are more granular and might not exactly align with the pre-defined rows of the static playbook, though they follow the same underlying efficiency logic.

Hey [~accountid:622b6eb2302c6b006af70509] Thanks for sending over the details.

As you know, Bolt drivers are engaged as independent contractors, so providing a pack that feels more like an employee-style welcome could be risky - especially as Bolt is actively defending its independent contractor model. Branded merchandise, in particular, may suggest a level of integration into Bolt’s business, which is a factor linked to worker status.

That said, if this is a one-off and the items are practical (like a phone mount, air freshener, or car charger), I think you can proceed +*as long as*+ the following steps are followed:

* Please{color:#bf2600} {color}{color:#bf2600}+*do not*+{color} include any Bolt-branded clothing or uniform-like items (e.g. t-shirts, hoodies, caps), as these are *high-risk*.
* Avoid calling it a “welcome pack.” Instead, go with something more neutral like “activation kit”, which sounds more business-oriented and less employee-style.
* Any messages to drivers should reflect this tone, for example: _“This activation kit includes items to help you get started with providing services via the Bolt platform”_, rather than anything that implies Bolt is “welcoming” them into the company.

Do not hesitate to reach out to me to discuss further, let me know if you have any questions!

Query for E-platform's information file:

{noformat}WITH thai_drivers_active AS (
  SELECT 
    fd.company_id,
    fd.id,
    fdr.personal_code,  
    fdr.first_name,
    fdr.last_name, 
    e.sum_with_vat,
    e.transaction_type,
    e.transaction_subtype,
    fc.country,
    e.reporting_local_date
  FROM ng_public_spark.etl_billing_balance_driver_v2 e
  LEFT JOIN ng_public_spark.fleet_driver fd 
    ON fd.id = e.entity_id
  LEFT JOIN ng_public_spark.fleet_company fc 
    ON fc.id = fd.company_id
  LEFT JOIN ng_public_spark.fleet_driver_root fdr
    ON fdr.id = fd.driver_root_id
  WHERE e.reporting_local_date BETWEEN DATE '2024-01-01' AND DATE '2024-12-31'
    AND fc.country = 'th' 
    AND e.entity_type = 'driver'
),
last_invoice AS (
  SELECT 
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
      PARTITION BY period_end_date, from_agent_type, from_agent_id, to_agent_type, to_agent_id 
      ORDER BY invoice_id DESC
    ) AS row_num,
    *
  FROM ng_public_spark.etl_billing_invoicing_rides_driver_commission
  WHERE period_end_date BETWEEN DATE '2024-01-01' AND DATE '2024-12-31'
),
commission_fee AS (
select partners.personal_code,
  ROUND(SUM(sum_with_vat)) AS commission_fee_amount
from last_invoice
LEFT JOIN ng_public_spark.fleet_driver drivers
ON drivers.id = last_invoice.to_agent_id
LEFT JOIN ng_public_spark.fleet_driver_root partners
ON partners.id = drivers.driver_root_id
GROUP BY personal_code
),
detailed_report AS(
SELECT DISTINCT
  active.personal_code AS national_ID,
  '' AS foreign_ID,
  '' AS title_of_business_operator,
  active.first_name AS name_of_operator,
  '' AS middle_name_of_operator,
  active.last_name AS last_name_of_operator,
  ROUND(SUM(
    CASE 
      WHEN active.reporting_local_date BETWEEN DATE '2024-01-01' AND DATE '2024-12-31' 
      AND active.transaction_type = 'ride_fee'
      THEN active.sum_with_vat 
      ELSE 0 
    END
  )) AS comission_base, 
    commission_fee_amount, 
  0 AS total_processing_payment_base,
  0 AS total_processing_payment_fee,
ROUND(SUM(
    CASE 
      WHEN active.reporting_local_date BETWEEN invoices.period_start_date AND invoices.period_end_date 
          AND active.transaction_type = 'fee' 
          AND active.transaction_subtype IN ('InstantPayoutFee', 'CustomFee')
      THEN ABS(active.sum_with_vat)
      WHEN active.reporting_local_date BETWEEN invoices.period_start_date AND invoices.period_end_date 
          AND active.transaction_type = 'fee' 
          AND active.transaction_subtype = 'ReverseInstantPayoutFee'
      THEN -ABS(active.sum_with_vat)
      ELSE 0 
    END
  )) AS other_income,
  'I' AS information_status
FROM thai_drivers_active active
LEFT JOIN last_invoice invoices
  ON invoices.to_agent_id = active.id
LEFT JOIN ng_public_spark.admin_system_city admin
    ON admin.id = invoices.city_id
LEFT JOIN commission_fee commission
    ON commission.personal_code = active.personal_code
  WHERE 
  invoices.to_agent_type = 'ride_hailing_driver' 
  AND invoices.invoice_type != 'credit_note' 
  AND admin.country_code IN ('th')
  AND invoices.row_num = 1
  GROUP BY 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9,10,12),
headers AS(
  SELECT
  'C' AS control,
  TO_CHAR(CURRENT_DATE, 'yyyyMMdd') AS report_delivery_date,
  0105565075610 AS platform_operator_ID,
  '' AS service_provider_ID,
  TO_CHAR((date_trunc('year', CURRENT_DATE) - INTERVAL '1 year')::date, 'yyyyMMdd') AS period_start_date,
  TO_CHAR((date_trunc('year', CURRENT_DATE) - INTERVAL '1 day')::date, 'yyyyMMdd') AS period_end_date,
  COUNT(*) AS nr_of_rows,
  ROUND(SUM (comission_base),2) AS total_commission_base,
  ROUND(SUM (commission_fee_amount)) AS total_commission_fee_amount, 
  0 AS total_processing_payment_base,
  0 AS total_processing_payment_fee,
  SUM (other_income) AS total_other_income
  FROM detailed_report
)
select * from headers
union all
select * from detailed_report{noformat}

Query for Business operator’s bank account numbers file:

{noformat}WITH 
thai_drivers_active AS (
SELECT DISTINCT entity_id 
FROM ng_public_spark.etl_billing_balance_driver_v2 e
LEFT JOIN ng_public_spark.fleet_driver fd ON fd.id = e.entity_id
LEFT JOIN ng_public_spark.fleet_company fc ON fc.id = fd.company_id
WHERE reporting_local_date BETWEEN DATE '2024-01-01' AND DATE '2024-12-31'
AND fc.country = 'th' 
AND e.entity_type = 'driver'),

profile_iban AS ( --filters IBANs registered on driver profiles
  SELECT DISTINCT
    partners.personal_code, 
    drivers.account_iban,   
    drivers.account_recipient, 
    drivers.account_swift     
  FROM ng_public_spark.fleet_driver drivers
  LEFT JOIN ng_public_spark.fleet_driver_root partners
  ON drivers.driver_root_id = partners.id
),
payout_iban AS ( -- filters IBANs used for payouts
SELECT DISTINCT
        partners.personal_code,
        ipca.account_recipient,
        ipca.account_iban,
        ipca.account_swift
    FROM ng_payout_spark.invoicing_payment_payout ipp
    LEFT JOIN ng_payout_spark.invoicing_payment_client ipc 
    on ipc.id = ipp.client_id
    LEFT JOIN ng_public_spark.fleet_driver drivers 
    on drivers.id = ipc.external_id
    LEFT JOIN ng_public_spark.fleet_driver_root AS partners
    ON drivers.driver_root_id = partners.id 
    LEFT JOIN ng_public_spark.fleet_company fc 
    on drivers.id = drivers.company_id
    LEFT JOIN ng_payout_spark.invoicing_payment_client_account ipca 
    on ipp.account_id = ipca.id
    LEFT JOIN ng_public_spark.admin_system_city sc 
    on sc.id = fc.city_id
    WHERE ipp.state = 'finished' 
        and date(from_utc_timestamp(ipp.created, sc.timezone)) between date '2024-01-01' and date '2024-12-31'
),
all_iban AS (
  SELECT personal_code, account_recipient, account_iban, account_swift
  FROM profile_iban

  UNION

  SELECT personal_code, account_recipient, account_iban, account_swift
  FROM payout_iban
),

detailed_report AS
(
SELECT DISTINCT
partners.personal_code AS national_ID,
'' AS foreign_ID,
all_iban.account_iban AS bank_acc_nr,
COALESCE(all_iban.account_recipient, '') AS bank_acc_name,
all_iban.account_swift AS SWIFT,
"I" AS information_status,
'' as empty
FROM ng_public_spark.fleet_driver AS drivers
LEFT JOIN ng_public_spark.fleet_company AS companies
    ON drivers.company_id = companies.id
LEFT JOIN ng_public_spark.fleet_driver_root AS partners
    ON drivers.driver_root_id = partners.id 
INNER JOIN thai_drivers_active
    ON drivers.id = thai_drivers_active.entity_id
LEFT JOIN all_iban
    ON all_iban.personal_code = partners.personal_code
),
headers as 
(
  SELECT 
'C' AS control,
TO_CHAR(CURRENT_DATE, 'yyyyMMdd') AS report_delivery_date,
0105565075610 AS platform_operator_ID,
'' AS service_provider_ID,
TO_CHAR((date_trunc('year', CURRENT_DATE) - INTERVAL '1 year')::date, 'yyyyMMdd') AS period_start_date,
TO_CHAR((date_trunc('year', CURRENT_DATE) - INTERVAL '1 day')::date, 'yyyyMMdd') AS period_end_date,
COUNT(*) AS nr_of_rows
FROM detailed_report
)
select * from headers
union all
select * from detailed_report{noformat}

* <> Okai ENG: Chip damage refers to the burning out of the power supply chip or TVS transistor (protection power supply chip) inside the IOT due to high current impact, which is manifested by the failure of the IOT to supply power normally, the indicator light is bad, and the device cannot be identified. The specific damage situation needs to be analyzed after obtaining the IOT defective parts.
* <> Okai business side: Not their problem. They can support us in finding out and testing, but as these IOTs were out of warranty they will not compensate us.

{quote}I do not agree that this is not their problem. These IOTs are used with OKAIs own HW/electronics and not with any other devices. If we have such significant QTY of IOTs which are encountering the same failure mode (~72%), then clearly it is something for which design could be improved or something which has not been well-tested with our use case (all our different HWs/FWs). Failure to pull down CANON is one of the main areas of troubleshooting our mechanics have to do, and very often it is solved by replacing only the IOT. If the IOT CAN chips are damaged more frequently than the rest of electronics, then there is a design/manufacturing error allowing for the CAN chips to burn or other electronic components are causing the IOT to fail. Either way, every electronic device we use on board of OKAI vehicles are from OKAI and no other supplier, so these issues originate from OKAI design. {quote}

For the rest of the items, it is more-less clear that the issues are related to SIM statuses or corrosion on the SIM card contacts, I have no good arguments.

Hi [~accountid:6054ecc4e394c30069d997f1] Unfortunately, it's not legally possible to amend the Terms & Conditions (T&Cs) retroactively; any changes can only apply moving forward.​

Our current T&Cs include the following clause:​

*_9.9._* _If the General Terms are terminated between the parties, the Delivery Partner undertakes to return to Bolt the thermo-bag_ *_provided by Bolt_* _within 3 business days from the date of termination. If the thermo-bag is not returned duly or not in good order, Bolt has the right to keep the deposit charged from the Delivery Partner for the thermo-bag.​_

This clause specifically pertains to thermo-bags supplied by Bolt and does not extend to those acquired from third-party suppliers.​

For thermo-bags provided by Bolt, if a communication was previously sent to all fleets instructing them to return the bags by a specified deadline, it's important to refer to that communication rather than the T&Cs.​

*Suggested Responses:*

* *For thermo-bags not purchased from Bolt:*
"Unfortunately, since your thermo-bag was purchased from [Third-Party Supplier Name] and not supplied by Bolt, we are unable to accept its return or refund your deposit."​
* *For thermo-bags purchased from Bolt:*
"Unfortunately, the deadline to return your Bolt-supplied thermo-bag was [Specified Date], as communicated to all fleets on [Communication Date]. Since the bag was not returned by that deadline, we are unable to process a return or refund your deposit."​

If such a communication was sent to the fleets, please reference that specific email in your response.​

Additionally, what we can do is just to remove this clause from T&Cs, but cannot specify that it applies from September 2024.

*Let’s Talk Compliance: what’s changing and how you are involved*

Hi Team,

We’re kicking off an important project to help us get a clearer picture of our compliance landscape. Don’t worry: this isn’t about throwing rules at you or burying you in legal jargon. It's about *making sure we know what really matters for our business*, how we’re doing, and where we might need to take action.

h3. 🧩 What’s This All About?

Over the past weeks, I’ve been *analysing frameworks, internal documentation (legal questionnaires and existing register), and various other sources* to extract possible relevant compliance requirements. Some laws were already known and documented, others were newly discovered through research. Now, we’re at the next step: validating and organising this information with your help.

The big goals:

* ✅ Confirm whether the identified requirements are *relevant* to our business 
* 📂 Understand our current *compliance status*
* 🧾 Identify what *evidence* already exists (or if we need to find it)
* ⚠️ Assess the *risks* tied to any missing or unclear areas

h3. 📁 How It’s Organised in Jira

We’re using *Jira* to keep everything structured and transparent:

* *Each sub-department* has its own *Epic*
* Inside each Epic are *Tasks* - each one represents a specific compliance requirement
* Your part is to help *review what’s already been mapped* and tell us if it applies to your area, if we’re compliant, and if you have any supporting documents or insights

This isn’t about adding work - it’s about *leveraging what you already know or do*, and filling in any missing pieces together.

h3. 🙌 Why This Matters

This project helps us:

* Avoid surprises from audits or regulatory changes
* Understand where we’re solid, and where we might need to act
* Build a centralised, smart system—so we’re not duplicating efforts or digging through scattered files

----

h3. 💬 What’s Next?

Over the next weeks, I’ll reach out to each sub-department to walk through your Epic in Jira. We’ll go over the tasks together—you’ll never be left on your own to figure it out.

If you have any questions in the meantime, just ping me.
Thanks so much for being part of this!

*Mitigation*

To ensure all PRs trigger their deployment workflow, the merge queue was reconfigured to allow only one PR to be merged at a time. This guarantees:

* Each merge creates a distinct push event.
* Every PR results in a deployment workflow run.

The {{main}} branch protection was adjusted to allow only 1 PR to merge at a time (down from 5).

h3. *Potential Side Effects*

* *Lower merge throughput* due to serialized merges.
* *Increased CI/CD activity*, with more frequent deployments and workflow runs.
* *Longer wait times* in the queue during periods of high PR volume.

Requirements have changed over time. I am pasting here the original requirements only for context:

[DEPRECATED REQUIREMENTS]

We need to ensure that we have a single source of truth for these key data points, and for each order ID we shall store the following information:

* {{initial_preparation_time_seconds}}*_:_* ML predicted food prep time duration.
* {{proposed_initial_preparation_time_seconds}}*_:_* The preparation time that we showed to the merchant when we proposed the order to them.
** If ML enabled & not busy -> same as _initial_preparation_time_seconds_
** If ML enabled &  busy -> _initial_preparation_time_seconds_ + _seconds_added_due_to_busy_mode_
** If ML disabled (or new provider) & not busy -> agreed prep time from Menu Manager (MM)
** If ML disabled &  busy -> agreed prep time from Menu Manager (MM)+ _seconds_added_due_to_busy_mode_
* {{initial_total_eta_input_preparation_time_seconds:}}The preparation time that we sent as an input to the Total ETA model on order creation.
** If ML enabled: proposed__initial_preparation_time_seconds_ (not the one shown to provider)
** If ML disabled: agreed prep time from Menu Manager (MM)+ _seconds_added_due_to_busy_mode_
* {{provider_adjusted_preparation_time_seconds}}*_:_* The preparation time that the merchant accepted the order with (so either the selected prep time if they adjusted it when accepting the order, or the initially shown prep time).
* {{provider_adjustment_seconds}}: Delta between {{initial_total_eta_input_preparation_time_seconds}} and {{provider_adjusted_preparation_time_seconds}}, essentially how much time did the provider add to the initially proposed preparation time.
* {{provider_adjusted_total_eta_input_preparation_time_seconds:}}The preparation time that we sent as an input to the Total ETA model on provider acceptance.
** If ML enabled: {{provider_adjusted_preparation_time_seconds}}
** If ML disabled: We still calculate initial ML food prep time and use {{initial_preparation_time_seconds}} (not MM or adjusted MM).
* {{courier_optimal_time_input_preparation_time_seconds:}} The preparation time that we sent as an input to the Optimal Courier Arrival Time model
** If ML enabled: {{provider_adjusted_preparation_time_seconds}}
** If ML disabled:  provider adjusted prep time from Menu Manager (MM)
* {{courier_optimal_time_output_preparation_time_seconds:}}Time based on which we try to dispatch couriers. Pickup delays should be calculated based on this value.
* {{courier_target_arrival_time_seconds}}: In cases when we do not manage to find a courier who would be able to reach provider at _courier_optimal_time_output_preparation_time_seconds_ (supply issues) the {{courier_target_arrival_ts != courier_optimal_time_output_preparation_time_seconds.}} In the scenarios let’s save the target arrival time duration for the first accepted courier.
* {{courier_target_arrival_time_at}}:  Target arrival timestamp for the first accepted courier.
* {{merchant_contractual_preparation_time_seconds}}: The Admin preparation time of the provider.
** Applicable for new providers and ML disabled providers but I think all providers might have it?
* {{seconds_added_due_to_busy_mode}}_:_ The number value of the additional minutes added on top of the preparation time due to busy mode (if activated for the order).
* {{is_ML_disabled}}: Boolean [true,false] that shows whether ML was disabled or not (the “Disable ETA correction” flag on provider profile).
* {{proposed_preparation_start_time_to_provider_at}}: Timestamp when we want them to start prepping food (when the notification was sent)
* {{actual_merchant_starts_preparation_at}}: Timestamp when they started to prep food (can we see this?).
* {{estimated_merchant_ends_preparation_at}}: Timestamp when we predict them to end prepping food
** If proposed_at = {{estimated_merchant_starts_preparation_at}}  -> predicted end timestamp at the time when order is proposed to provider.
** If proposed_at < {{estimated_merchant_starts_preparation_at}}  -> predicted end timestamp at the time when we send “start preparing” notification.
* {{actual_merchant_ends_preparation_at}}: Timestamp when they finished food prep.
* {{actual_preparation_duration_seconds}}: Actual food prep time duration
* {{provider_preparation_adjustment_seconds}}: difference between proposed and accepted food prep durations.
* {{dispatch_flow_type}}: I’m not sure about the name, but it should show if it’s parallel, auto-optimised or courier-first flow.
* {{is_integrated_provider}}: Boolean [true,false].
* {{delivery_type: }}[platform, pickup, ROD, robot]

*Gemini’s summary of the interactions between* [*Getaround terms*|https://docs.google.com/document/d/10YgcZ2WJVsaWwEkmTzR8yU4M2X3Y7S7ZWi9Q9Se3ml4/edit?tab=t.0] *and specific conditions established by car owners in the rental agreements entered between them and renters:*

Here's an outline of the excerpts and provisions dealing with the completion of Getaround terms by the rental agreement between users and owners, and how Getaround ensures consistency:

# *Terms and Rental Agreement as a Combined Agreement:*

* The document states that "The Rentals are governed by the present Terms and are completed by the Rental Agreements."
* It emphasizes that "Only by complying with the Terms together with the Rental Agreement can Users benefit from the Services offered by Getaround."
* This indicates that both the general Getaround Terms and the specific Rental Agreement for each rental work together as a binding agreement.

# *Content of the Rental Agreement:*

* The Rental Agreement captures essential information at the beginning and end of each rental, including:
** Mileage
** Fuel level
** Visible damage (exterior and interior)
** Vehicle cleanliness
* This ensures a record of the vehicle's condition at the start and end of the rental, helping to resolve disputes and determine responsibility for any damage.

# *Types of Rental Agreements:*

* Rental Agreements can be:
** Hard copy (paper)
** Electronic via the App (for both Connect and non-Connect rentals)
* Regardless of the format, the Rental Agreement is a crucial part of the overall rental agreement.

# *Role of Getaround in the Rental Agreement Process:*

* For Connect rentals, Getaround's system automatically collects data like mileage and fuel level.
* Getaround provides the platform and tools for completing Rental Agreements (especially the App).
* Getaround sets the general Terms that all users must adhere to.

# *Car Owner's Specific Rules and Conditions:*

* Car Owners can add specific rules and conditions for their vehicle rentals, but these must be within limits:
** They can concern minimum age, license duration, smoking, pets, maximum rental duration, and delivery of the vehicle.
** They cannot involve unjustified discrimination or conditions contrary to applicable laws or the Getaround Terms.
* This allows for some flexibility for Car Owners while ensuring they don't contradict Getaround's overall Terms.

# *Consistency and Enforcement:*

* The Getaround Terms act as the overarching framework. Car Owners' specific conditions are additions, not replacements, and must align with the Terms.
* Getaround reserves the right to refuse or exclude any vehicle that does not comply with the Terms.
* Getaround provides tools and processes (like the Rental Agreement) to document and enforce compliance with the Terms.
* Disputes are handled within the context of both the Terms and the Rental Agreement.

*In essence:*

Getaround ensures consistency by having a set of comprehensive Terms and Conditions that all users must agree to. The Rental Agreement then supplements these Terms with specific details of each rental. Car Owners can add some specific rules, but these cannot override the general Terms. Getaround provides the platform and tools to facilitate this process and enforce compliance.

Summary of [~accountid:612f31d89976c300693ebaf7] suggestions:

(i) It makes sense that the ['indicative factors' you collectively put together |https://docs.google.com/document/d/1C-cKYNFhE3DYsoi8cR983JVd84ejecCt/edit]get matched against the GOAT rating system (see the image) - this works and can help ensure uniformity of approach

!Screenshot 2025-04-02 at 15.35.51 (1).png|width=1800,height=1206,alt="Screenshot 2025-04-02 at 15.35.51 (1).png"!

(ii) The other thing to align on was *“when should GFT suggest to finance that we might need to provision”?*

*Position from finance:* we *must* provision when we *expect* a loss (>50%). We must also disclose contingent losses (10-50%) but no need to provision.

*Question for LRP:* When does Bolt *expect* a ‘reclass related loss’?

*Answer*: (i) when we *expect* to get claims (or have got claims) *_and_* (ii) we *expect* to lose those claims.We can give that “shape” as follows:

* (i) Do we think it’s more than 50% likely that we are going to face claims/regulatory action in the next five years? YES / NO / UNSURE
* (ii) if the answer to (i) is YES, do we think it’s more than 50% likely that we are going to lose those claims? YES / NO / UNSURE

If the answer to those questions is anything other than YES, then it’s clearly 'not expected’ (<50%).

As part of those questions there is no need to be precise in respect of ‘how many claims’ etc. as figuring out what ought to be provisioned (if anything) is a subsequent step involving the finance team, although relevant factors to help steer that later step would be:

* How many claimants
* How far back can they claim
* Will the pool of claimants reduct over time
* Scope for settlement
* Impact of fleets?
* Can ‘class action’ claims take place

^^^ that's the basis on which I've suggested we can reduce the existing provisioning for NL (which makes sense because they are currently provisioning 100% for 100% of drivers, which is too much).

Possible solutions:

# Decouple tests from actual resource (S3 bucket) by {{mocking all S3-related calls}}, similar to how we mock network or DB APIs.
# Consolidate all comp tests using the same S3 bucket under a {{single comp test file}}. It’s not a proper fix, more like a workaround/hack, prone to future mistakes.
# Add support in testing framework to {{explicitly mark test cases that should not be parallelized}}. Would require constant attention from the product teams to mark their tests correctly. Technically would work, but it’s guaranteed to have mistakes and for the race condition to occur.
# {{Automatic detection of non-parallelizable tests}} base on S3 buckets referenced by test configuration. Guaranteed to work, requires no input from product teams.
# {{Virtualize S3 bucket access}} for {{LOCAL}} and {{TEST}} environments at framework level: multiple tests may require access to the same S3 bucket, but the framework opaquely adds a prefix to forward them to unique S3 buckets. Complexity downside: all API calls must hide this redirection from the user code.
# Add a {{global lock for exclusive access to S3 buckets}} in the test framework. Tests would be written without any explicit synchronization in the user code, synchronization happens at framework level. It has the same effect as options 3 and 4, but different implementation.
